description:
Before any language work, find out what a portable vector type would buy and cost.

- Ceiling: hand-write two SIMD algorithms in C with GCC/Clang vector extensions (__attribute__((vector_size)), __builtin_shufflevector), not per-arch intrinsics, compiled for portable and architecture targets: simdutf8-style UTF-8 validation (vs examples/utf8_valid.exs and String.valid?) and a SIMD substring search (vs :binary.match). Measure; this bounds what a defk vector type could reach.
- Design sketch (no implementation): a lane type (e.g. v128 of u8/i32/f64, or a width chosen at build time), element-wise ops, lane reductions, shuffles/table lookups, compares to masks, masked/tail-safe loads that keep the bounds guarantee. Elixir-mode semantics (lanes as tuples or binaries) and the cost of agreement properties per op. Float lane reductions vs bit-exactness. How it reads as Elixir.
- Compare with Zig @Vector, Wasm SIMD128, Rust portable_simd.

Done when the ceiling numbers and the design sketch are in docs/research/simd.md, with a recommendation (build it, defer it, or rule it out) for the decision ticket.
title: Research and ceiling study: portable vector values in the subset
